repo_notes.content: The repository provides reference configurations and examples for deploying Camunda 8 on STACKIT. It expands the official Camunda Deployment References with specific instructions, infrastructure templates, and best practices for STACKIT. The main documentation can be found in the README.md

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the Camunda 8 on STACKIT deployment project: what it does, why it exists, the overall architecture, and how the repository is organized. Links to child pages for setup and architecture details.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for onboarding engineers: prerequisites, STACKIT CLI authentication, service account creation, S3 backend bootstrapping, and running the first terraform init/apply cycle.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Detailed description of the layered architecture: STACKIT cloud foundation, Terraform orchestration layer, Kubernetes (SKE) compute layer, and Camunda 8 application layer. Covers the Mermaid diagram in docs/architecture-overview.mermaid and how all services relate to each other.

pages.title: Contributing and Issue Reporting
pages.purpose: Explains the GitHub contribution workflow, how to use the bug report and feature request issue templates, and the pull request process.

pages.title: Environment Configuration
pages.purpose: Overview of how environments are structured and configured in this repository, linking to child pages covering the single-region environment layout, provider/version pinning, and example configuration files.

pages.title: Single-Region Environment
pages.purpose: Deep dive into the single-region environment: the main.tf orchestration file, module wiring, dependency graph between infrastructure modules, and how the environment provisions the full Camunda stack end-to-end.

pages.title: Provider and Version Configuration
pages.purpose: Covers versions.tf: Terraform version lock (1.16.3), provider version constraints (stackit ~>0.117, helm, kubernetes, kubectl, vault), S3 backend configuration, and the provider dependency chain that ties SKE and Secrets Manager outputs to application-layer providers.

pages.title: Input Variables and Example Configuration
pages.purpose: Reference for all input variables defined in variables.tf: project_id, dns_name, environment, SKE sizing, Zeebe cluster topology, Keycloak admin, PostgreSQL flavor/storage, OpenSearch plan, and Web Modeler mail. Includes annotated terraform.tfvars.example and config.s3.example.tfbackend.

pages.title: Terraform Modules
pages.purpose: Overview of the reusable Terraform modules under modules/. Introduces the two categories — STACKIT infrastructure modules and Kubernetes application modules — and links to child pages for each group.

pages.title: Camunda Workflow Engine Module
pages.purpose: Detailed documentation of the camunda-workflow-engine module: Helm chart deployment, Zeebe cluster topology configuration, OpenSearch integration (replacing Elasticsearch), OIDC authentication via Keycloak, Gateway API routes and Envoy policies for web and gRPC endpoints, and secret management via ExternalSecret resources.

pages.title: Identity Management Modules
pages.purpose: Covers the two Keycloak-related modules: keycloak-operator-bootstrap (CRD installation, operator deployment from remote URLs, namespace setup) and kubernetes-identity-management (Keycloak CR configuration, PostgreSQL backend, HTTPRoute, bootstrapAdmin secret wiring).

pages.title: STACKIT Infrastructure Modules
pages.purpose: Documents the STACKIT-specific infrastructure modules: stackit-ske (Kubernetes cluster provisioning, node pools, Flatcar OS, kubeconfig decoding), stackit-postgres (PostgreSQL Flex instance, user, database iteration, ACL), stackit-opensearch (OpenSearch instance, credentials, ACL), stackit-dns (DNS zone), and stackit-object-storage (S3 bucket, credentials group).

pages.title: Kubernetes Platform Modules
pages.purpose: Documents the Kubernetes-layer platform modules: kubernetes-gateway (Envoy Gateway as the Gateway API implementation, cert-manager with Gateway API support, STACKIT cert-manager DNS-01 webhook, a Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer), kubernetes-gateway-app (per-application EnvoyProxy and Gateway with HTTPS listeners, TLS via cert-manager and DNS via the ExternalDNS annotation on the Envoy Service), kubernetes-secret-management (External Secrets Operator Helm chart and the ClusterSecretStore for STACKIT Secrets Manager), kubernetes-messaging (NATS Helm chart, namespace), and stackit-secrets-manager (STACKIT Secrets Manager instance and user).

pages.title: Secret Management Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the end-to-end secret management strategy used across the deployment, linking to child pages covering the Vault/STACKIT Secrets Manager integration and the External Secrets Operator pattern.

pages.title: STACKIT Secrets Manager and Vault Integration
pages.purpose: Explains how the STACKIT Secrets Manager (Vault-compatible) is provisioned, how a service user is created with write access, how the kubernetes-secret-management module stores its password in a Kubernetes Secret and configures the ClusterSecretStore with userpass authentication against the STACKIT Vault endpoint.

pages.title: External Secrets Operator and ExternalSecret Resources
pages.purpose: Covers the External Secrets Operator (ESO) deployment, the ClusterSecretStore resource, and how ExternalSecret manifests are used to synchronize Vault KV secrets into Kubernetes namespaces. Details the four ExternalSecret resources in the camunda-workflow-engine module: camunda-passwords, opensearch-credentials, postgres-webmodeler-credentials, and keycloak-initial-admin-credentials.

pages.title: Networking and TLS
pages.purpose: Overview of the networking architecture: how external traffic reaches the cluster, how DNS is managed, and how TLS certificates are issued. Links to child pages on the Gateway API and DNS.

pages.title: Gateway API and TLS Certificate Management
pages.purpose: Details the kubernetes-gateway module: Envoy Gateway (Gateway API) Helm deployment with its CRDs and GatewayClass, cert-manager Helm deployment with CRDs and Gateway API support enabled, the STACKIT cert-manager DNS-01 webhook (service account key Secret, Helm release) and a Let's Encrypt ClusterIssuer using the DNS-01 webhook solver, and the dependency chain ensuring correct provisioning order. Covers the kubernetes-gateway-app module, which creates one EnvoyProxy and Gateway per application (camunda-gateway, keycloak-gateway) with TLS secrets (camunda-gateway-tls, keycloak-gateway-tls) issued by cert-manager and DNS records created from the ExternalDNS hostname annotation on the Envoy LoadBalancer Service, and the routes and Envoy policies the camunda-workflow-engine and kubernetes-identity-management modules attach to these Gateways.

pages.title: DNS Zone and SKE DNS Extension
pages.purpose: Covers the stackit-dns module (stackit_dns_zone resource), how the DNS zone is wired to the SKE cluster's DNS extension, and how the dns_name variable drives the hostnames for all Camunda components and Keycloak.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Definitions of all codebase-specific terms, abbreviations, STACKIT service names, Camunda component names, and Terraform/Kubernetes patterns used throughout the repository. Each entry includes file path references for engineers onboarding to the project.
